record.context_brief: A priori L-infinity bounds in the very soft potential case
record.original_question: In the space-homogeneous Boltzmann or Landau equation with gamma + 2s < 0, can one obtain an a priori L-infinity bound for classical solutions? The paper presents this missing estimate as the key obstruction in the very soft potential case.

evidence.quote: Regularity estimates for the space homogeneous problem face a strong limitation when γ + 2s < 0. This range is called the very soft potential case. The Landau equation corresponds to s = 1, thus very soft potentials are those with γ < −2. Note that the very soft potential range is excluded from Theorems 3.1 and 3.2.The problem is that, even in the space homogeneous scenario, we do not know how to obtain an a priori estimate for the solution in L∞ when γ + 2s < 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation without angular cutoff, or the spatially homogeneous Landau equation, on $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d\ge 3$), for an unknown $f=f(t,v)\ge 0$:
$$\partial_t f = Q(f,f),$$
where $Q$ is either the non-cutoff Boltzmann collision operator with kinetic factor $|v-v_*|^\gamma$ and angular singularity of order $2s$ (so the collision kernel behaves like $|v-v_*|^\gamma b(\cos\theta)$ with $b(\cos\theta)\sin^{d-2}\theta \sim \theta^{-(d-1)-2s}$ as $\theta\to 0$, with $\gamma\in(-d,1]$, $s\in(0,1)$), or the Landau collision operator (formally the case $s=1$) with kinetic factor $|v-v_*|^{\gamma+2}$, $\gamma\in[-d,1]$.

Assume the initial datum $f_0\ge 0$ has finite mass, energy, and entropy, and is smooth and rapidly decaying. Assume one works in the "very soft potential" regime
$$\gamma + 2s < 0$$
(which for the Landau equation, $s=1$, corresponds to $\gamma<-2$, including the Coulomb case $\gamma=-3$ in $d=3$).

Question: Does there exist an a priori estimate of the form
$$\|f(t,\cdot)\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)} \le C(t,f_0)<\infty\qquad \text{for all } t>0,$$
for every classical solution, depending only on the initial mass, energy, entropy (and possibly higher moments) of $f_0$, with no further conditional integrability assumption on $f$?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works obtain L^∞ bounds only conditionally: assuming a priori control of suitable L^p moments (Prodi–Serrin-type criteria) or higher integrability of the solution. For the very soft potential range γ+2s<0, including the Landau–Coulomb case, an unconditional a priori L^∞ estimate depending only on initial mass/energy/entropy is not known and is still regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Conditional integrability and stability for the homogeneous Boltzmann equation with very soft potentials
status_evidence.snippet: A practical criterion that justifies the propagation and appearance of L^p-norms for solutions to the spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation with very soft potentials without cutoff is introduced...
status_evidence.claim: L^∞/L^p control is only available conditionally in the very soft potential regime.

status_evidence.title: A Priori Estimates for Solutions to the Landau Equation Under Prodi–Serrin Like Criteria
status_evidence.snippet: Prodi–Serrin like criteria are introduced which enable a priori estimates for the spatially homogeneous Landau equation for all classical soft potentials, including the Coulomb case.
status_evidence.claim: A priori estimates in the very soft/Coulomb regime currently require additional conditional integrability hypotheses.
